tasks.instruction_text: I'm scoping a AWS workload for a customer in us-east-1 (N. Virginia) — set up a quote for Amazon EC2 (m5.large On-Demand), override the default usage to 1460 VM-hours (2 VMs always-on) for the month, and pin the Business Support tier since this is a regulated tenant.
Could you put together a AWS Lambda quote? Always-on 1-month workload — use 10M API calls — and bill it out of us-east-2 (Ohio), the Developer Support tier is fine, we don't need anything fancier.
Need to estimate Amazon RDS (db.m5.large MySQL) sitting in us-west-2 (Oregon) at about 100 DB-hours. We're on the Basic Support tier anyway.
Configure the calculator for Amazon CloudFront in us-west-1 (N. California) — usage around 500 GB storage per month and we're already on the Enterprise On-Ramp tier for the FedRAMP tenant.
What's the projected monthly bill for Amazon Bedrock (Claude 3 Sonnet) in us-gov-west-1 (GovCloud) doing 10M input + 2M output tokens, with the Basic Support tier attached?
Quick check — if I put 1460 VM-hours (2 VMs always-on) through Amazon EC2 (m5.large On-Demand) in ca-central-1 (Canada), on the Basic Support tier, what does the monthly estimate come to?

Hmm, what would Amazon EC2 (m5.large On-Demand) cost me in sa-east-1 (São Paulo) for a 1460 VM-hours (2 VMs always-on) monthly commitment if I add the Business Support tier on top? Just want the number.

Pricing exercise for a finance review: configure the calculator for Amazon CloudFront in eu-west-1 (Ireland), override usage to 500 GB storage, leave support at the Basic Support tier, then tell me the all-in monthly total — they want it for the budget doc.

OK so I need to estimate AWS Lambda running in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) for one month — use 10M API calls — and we're on the Developer Support tier; set it up in the calculator and give me the monthly figure.

Hey, can you set up an estimate for 1460 VM-hours (2 VMs always-on) out of eu-west-2 (London) on Amazon EC2 (m5.large On-Demand) and tell me the monthly cost? We're on the Basic Support tier, but if it's over $1000/month we'll probably want to revisit.
